title: SSL, authentication and connection strings
question: The app cannot connect, or rejects the database certificate. Is it the connection string, the TLS settings, the credentials or the network path?

controls.purpose: A different, untrusted CA fails with the same certificate-chain code as no CA, so the code alone does not show which CA the client has.
A host name that is not on the certificate fails at the same stage with a different code.
Shows how the pinned driver treats sslmode=require: as a full certificate check, with a warning.
With uselibpqcompat=true the connection is encrypted but the certificate is not verified. This is a control, never a fix.
With TLS off, the server refuses the connection with SQLSTATE 28000, a server-side refusal rather than a client certificate error.
Fails with 28P01 after certificate verification passed.
Also fails with 28P01, so the client error alone cannot tell it from a wrong password.
Records how the parser handles # left unencoded in a password.
Records how the parser handles @ left unencoded in a password.
Records how the parser handles # and @ together, left unencoded.
The same password percent-encoded, as the working counterpart.
A port with nothing listening fails at TCP connect, before TLS or authentication.
